1.meaning: He glorified, extolled — the completed act of declaring something utterly free from all defect or imperfection; the root sense is wholeness/completeness, so to glorify is to declare the absolute perfection of the subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form II), third person masculine singular. The doubled middle consonant (tashdīd on bā') intensifies the root meaning. The final -a is the standard past-tense marker for a 'he' subject.
1.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to glorify, declare free of defect, swim (through)

2.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
2.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

6.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
6.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
6.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

9.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
9.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

10.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
10.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

11.meaning: The All-Wise — one possessing perfect wisdom, who puts everything in its right place and acts with flawless judgment; can also carry the sense of one who decrees and decides soundly.
11.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) stressing the depth and constancy of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a describing predicate.
11.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, to be wise

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: 'He brought out / expelled / drove out' — to make someone or something come out, the completed act of one male doer.
3.grammar: Past-tense verb in the causative pattern 'afʿala' ('akhraja' = to cause to go out). The bare stem with a final '-a' and no added subject marks a third-person masculine singular doer ('he') and a completed action.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
5.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
6.root: — (preposition)

7.meaning: People of / folk of / those belonging to — the family, followers, or possessors of something (as in 'people of the Book'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with a thing.
7.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/folk of'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('people OF …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.
7.root: ء-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, people belonging to

8.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
8.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: Their homes or dwellings; the places where they live. 'Diyār' is the plural of 'dār,' a house, abode, or region one inhabits.
10.grammar: A plural noun followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The -i vowel on the stem is the genitive case, here triggered by the attached possessor and typical after prepositions or in possessive linkage ('the homes of…').

11.meaning: At (the) first; combined from the preposition li- ('for/at') and awwal ('first/foremost'). Indicates the first occurrence, the first time, the initial instance.
11.grammar: A preposition (li-) followed by a noun in the genitive case. The -i ending on awwali is genitive, governed by the preposition.
11.root: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to precede (awwal is the elative/superlative form)

12.meaning: The gathering, the assembly, the mustering — used especially for the great eschatological gathering or for a military assembly; here it names the expulsion/exile as a 'gathering' or 'mustering out'.
12.grammar: A masculine noun in the genitive case; the -i ending is genitive, here governed by the preceding preposition (li-awwali l-ḥashri). The definite article al- marks it as a specific, known gathering.
12.root: ح-ش-ر (ḥ-sh-r) — to gather, muster, resurrect; the noun denotes a forced gathering or assembly

13.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
13.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

14.meaning: You (all) thought, supposed, assumed — the act of forming an opinion or expectation, often with an element of doubt or presumption rather than certain knowledge.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb, second person masculine plural. The -tum suffix is the standard marker for 'you all' (masculine) in the past tense. The doubled nūn (tashdīd) is characteristic of roots with a doubled middle letter.
14.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to think, suppose, assume, have an opinion (often without certainty)

15.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
15.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

16.meaning: They go out / depart / exit: to leave a place, to come or go forth from within.
16.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb of Form I, third-person masculine plural ('they go out'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject and the -ū ending marks a plural of males. The normally-final -na is dropped, signalling the subjunctive or jussive mood that follows certain particles.
16.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, to exit, to emerge

17.meaning: And they became convinced or sure, reaching a settled inner judgement — the verb spans 'to think/suppose' through 'to be certain.'
17.grammar: The connective 'wa' plus a past-tense verb. The '-ū' ending marks a masculine plural subject, 'they.' The doubled 'nn' belongs to the root.

18.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
18.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

19.meaning: Their fortresses (would have) defended them / their strongholds as protectors — the noun refers to something that prevents, blocks, or shields; here the fortresses are cast as active defenders.
19.grammar: A feminine active participle used as a noun ('the one that defends'), nominative case (-u ending), functioning as the subject of the clause. The attached pronoun -hum is the object ('them').
19.root: م-ن-ع (m-n-ʿ) — to prevent, restrain, defend, protect

20.meaning: Their fortresses, their strongholds — the plural of ḥiṣn (a fortified place, citadel, stronghold); the -hum suffix indicates possession.
20.grammar: A masculine plural noun in the nominative case; the -u ending is nominative (the fortresses are the subject). The plural ḥuṣūn is the broken (internal) plural of ḥiṣn.
20.root: ح-ص-ن (ḥ-ṣ-n) — to fortify, to be inaccessible; the noun ḥiṣn means a fortified stronghold

21.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
21.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

22.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
22.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

23.meaning: Then there came to them — the prefix fa- marks immediate consequence ('then, so'), and atā means 'came/arrived'. Together: 'and so (something) came to them'.
23.grammar: The fa- is a connective conjunction indicating result. Atā is a past-tense Form I verb, third person masculine singular; the weak final root letter (wāw/yā') contracts in the past tense. The enclitic -humu is the direct object pronoun.
23.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring; the past tense atā shows the characteristic contraction of a defective root

24.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
24.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

25.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
25.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

26.meaning: Wherever / in whatever place — an adverb pointing to an unspecified location, 'in the place where ...'.
26.grammar: An invariable adverb of place ('where / wherever'). Although it ends in -u, it is fixed in form and does not change for case; it is normally followed by a clause stating the situation tied to that place.

27.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

27.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

28.meaning: They expected, they calculated, they reckoned — the Form VIII of the root implies a reflexive or intensive reckoning/accounting; here it means they anticipated or counted on (something happening).
28.grammar: A present/imperfect verb (Form VIII), third person masculine plural, in the subjunctive mood (indicated by the absence of the final nūn after -ū). The subjunctive is triggered by the preceding lam of negation ('they did not expect').
28.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to count, reckon, consider; Form VIII (iḥtasaba) adds a reflexive/intensive sense of calculating for oneself

29.meaning: And He cast, He hurled, He threw — used figuratively for casting fear into hearts; the root conveys an act of throwing or projecting something with force.
29.grammar: The wāw is a connective conjunction ('and'). Qadhafa is a past-tense verb, Form I, third person masculine singular; the -a ending marks the completed past action of a 'he' subject.
29.root: ق-ذ-ف (q-dh-f) — to throw, hurl, cast; used figuratively for projecting fear or accusations

30.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
30.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

31.meaning: A noun meaning 'hearts' — the plural of the heart, understood as the inner seat of feeling, understanding, intention, and faith, not merely the physical organ.
31.grammar: A plural noun. The -i vowel on the stem is the genitive ending, which links the noun to what follows or follows a preposition ('… of …'); the attached -him(u) means 'their', so together it reads 'their hearts'. The final short -u is a connecting vowel that smooths pronunciation before the next word.

32.meaning: Terror, dread, intense fear — overwhelming fright that grips and unsettles a person. 'Ruʿb' is a fear that fills and shakes the heart.
32.grammar: A noun ('terror') with the -a ending, marking the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb ('… the terror'). With 'al-' ('the') it is definite. The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'r' (pronounced ar-ruʿba).
32.root: ر-ع-ب (r-ʿ-b) — to fill with dread, to terrify

33.meaning: They were demolishing, ruining, destroying their own houses — Form II of the root, which intensifies the simple meaning of destruction; the -ūna ending indicates ongoing action.
33.grammar: A present/imperfect verb (Form IV reading: yukhribu; or Form II: yukharribu — here Form II with tashdīd). Third person masculine plural; the -ūna suffix marks masculine plural present tense. The action was ongoing.
33.root: خ-ر-ب (kh-r-b) — to ruin, destroy, devastate; khariba means to fall into ruin; Form II yukharribu means to cause demolition actively

34.meaning: Their houses, their homes — the plural of bayt (a dwelling, house, household); -hum marks possession ('their').
34.grammar: A masculine plural noun in the accusative case; the -a ending is accusative, as the noun is the direct object of the demolishing action. Buyūt is the broken plural of bayt.
34.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to spend the night, to dwell; the noun bayt is a house or dwelling

35.meaning: 'With their hands.' The plural of yad ('hand') combined with the preposition 'with/by' and an attached pronoun 'their,' denoting physical handling or agency by the hands.
35.grammar: A plural noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by means of'), which places the noun in the genitive; the attached -him means 'their.' The -ī here belongs to the broken-plural stem aydī ('hands').
35.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — the hand; by extension, power, agency, means

36.meaning: And the hands (of) — the plural of yad (hand); used here in the phrase 'by their own hands and the hands of the believers'.
36.grammar: Wāw is a connective. Aydī is a defective (defective root) plural noun in the genitive case; the -ī ending is genitive, as the noun is in an iḍāfa (possessive construct) chain.
36.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand; the root is defective; yad is the singular, aydī the plural

37.meaning: Of the believers — the active participle of āmana (to believe/have faith), in the plural; refers to those who have accepted faith.
37.grammar: A masculine sound plural noun in the genitive case; the -īna ending (-ī + na) is the genitive/accusative form of the sound masculine plural (nominative would be -ūna). Here genitive as the second term of an iḍāfa.
37.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to believe; Form IV āmana means 'to believe'; the active participle mu'min means 'believer'

38.meaning: So take a lesson, reflect and learn — Form VIII imperative, conveying that one should cross over from apparent to hidden meaning, drawing a moral lesson from what has happened.

parts.en: take a lesson / reflect and learn

38.grammar: The fa- signals a command following from what preceded. Iʿtabirū is a Form VIII imperative, second person masculine plural; the final -ū is the masculine plural imperative suffix. The root's Form VIII sense is to cross over (ʿibra = crossing/lesson).
38.root: ع-ب-ر (ʿ-b-r) — to cross, to pass over; the noun ʿibra means a lesson drawn from crossing over from apparent to real meaning

39.meaning: 'O possessors of / O people endowed with …' — a vocative phrase calling out to those who hold or are characterized by something (e.g., 'O people of understanding'). 'ulī' means 'owners/possessors of'.
39.grammar: A call or address: 'yā' is the particle 'O!' used to summon or address someone. 'ulī' means 'those who possess / owners of' and is a plural noun used only in construct — it must be followed by another noun ('possessors OF …'). It is an irregular noun with no singular: its nominative is 'ulū' and its accusative/genitive (oblique) form is 'ulī'. The 'ī' here is that oblique form, the shape this word regularly takes when it leads a construct phrase like this; it is not caused by the call itself.
39.root: — (no triliteral root; 'yā' is a vocative particle and 'ulī' is a defective noun meaning 'possessors of')

40.meaning: 'eyesight, vision, insight' — the plural of the word for sight or the seeing faculty; the perceptions of the eyes, and by extension discernment.
40.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of baṣar ('sight, vision'), with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i marks the genitive case, which typically means the word is linked to a preceding noun ('… OF vision') or governed by a preposition. The root denotes seeing and, figuratively, insight.

1.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

1.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
2.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
2.root: — (particle; no root)

3.meaning: He wrote / decreed / prescribed: literally 'to write', and by extension to ordain, make obligatory, or settle something as a binding decree.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb of the basic Form I, third-person masculine singular ('he wrote/decreed'), shown by the bare -a ending. Beyond literal writing, it commonly means to prescribe or make something binding, as in a divine decree.
3.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; writing, decree, prescription

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
4.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: 'Upon them / against them' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') carrying an attached plural pronoun referring to a group of males.
5.grammar: ʿalā ('upon') takes the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The -him ending is the attached pronoun for a masculine plural 'them'; its final vowel appears as -u (himu) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with the definite article.

6.meaning: The exile, the expulsion, the going-forth — the noun form referring to the act of being sent out or driven out from one's home.
6.grammar: A masculine noun in the accusative case; the -a ending here functions as the accusative. The definite article al- marks a specific, known exile. Used as an object in the verbal clause.
6.root: ج-ل-و (j-l-w) — to go away, to be made clear/visible; the noun jalāʾ refers to the act of departing or being expelled from a homeland

7.meaning: He would certainly have punished them — the lam- prefix is an emphatic particle that with a past-tense verb indicates a hypothetical completed action ('would have'). ʿAdhdhabahum = He punished them.

parts.en: certainly (emphatic, with the sense of 'would have')

7.grammar: The lam- is a 'lam of the answer' (lam jawāb) used in a conditional context, implying a counterfactual: 'had this been the case, He would certainly have punished them.' ʿAddhaba is a Form II past-tense verb (third person masculine singular), with the object pronoun -hum.
7.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, to torment; Form II intensifies: to inflict severe punishment

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
9.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
9.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

10.meaning: 'And for them / and they have.' A combination expressing possession or entitlement belonging to a group of males: 'and to/for them (belongs).' The particle li- conveys 'for' or 'belonging to,' and the attached pronoun refers to 'them.'
10.grammar: A possessive/benefactive phrase: the preposition li- ('for, belonging to') with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them,' masculine plural). Such 'for X' phrases commonly express that something belongs to or is owed to that party.

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

12.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
12.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
12.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

13.meaning: A noun meaning 'punishment, torment, chastisement' — painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
13.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject or doer of a sentence (the thing performing or undergoing the main action) and is the noun's basic citation form.

14.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
14.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

1.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' — pointing to something distant (in space, time, or rank) rather than near. It singles out and draws attention to a far-off or already-mentioned referent.
1.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for a single masculine referent. It does not take case endings; the -ka element addresses the listener and the -li- signals distance, together yielding 'that' as opposed to the nearer 'this'.

2.meaning: That is because they — the combined form bi-annahum: the preposition bi- ('with/because of') + anna ('that') + hum ('they'). Together it introduces a causal clause: 'because they …'
2.grammar: Bi- is a preposition that here functions causally ('because of the fact that'). Anna is a strong complementizer that takes the following clause as its object (subjunctive noun clause). Hum is a detached pronoun serving as the subject of the anna clause.
2.root: — (no single root; this is a prepositional-complementizer phrase)

3.meaning: A connector meaning 'because they…' or 'by reason that they…'. It fuses the preposition bi- (here giving a cause, 'because of') with anna ('that', an emphatic particle introducing a fact) and the attached pronoun -hum ('they').
3.grammar: bi- here gives a causal sense ('because of'). anna is an emphatic particle meaning 'that' which introduces a statement of fact and takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; the attached -hum is that pronoun, a masculine plural 'they'. Together they give a reason: 'because they …'.

4.meaning: They opposed, resisted, or split off into hostile contention against someone — to set oneself in conflict with another, taking the opposing 'side' (shiqq).
4.grammar: A past-tense verb of the mutual/reciprocal pattern (form III), which adds the sense of acting against or toward another party — here 'to be in opposition with'. The -ū ending means the subject is 'they' (a masculine plural group) and the action is completed (past).
4.root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q) — to split, cleave; figuratively to break away into opposition, to be at odds

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
6.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching a messenger

7.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
7.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

8.meaning: Allah — the proper name of God in Islam, encompassing all divine attributes; not derived from a common noun but treated as a proper name that subsumes all the divine names.
8.grammar: The proper divine name in the accusative case; the -a ending is accusative, indicating it is the object of the verb (yushāqqi, 'opposes'). The definite article (al-) is intrinsic to the name.
8.root: — (the name is generally treated as a proper noun; some scholars link it to أ-ل-ه ʾ-l-h: to worship, to be a deity)

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
9.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

10.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
10.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: In punishment, in the penalty — the genitive of ʿiqāb (retribution, punishment, penalty); part of the divine name/attribute 'shadīd al-ʿiqāb' (severe in punishment).
12.grammar: A masculine noun in the genitive case; the -i ending is genitive, as it is the second term of the construct phrase shadīd al-ʿiqāb ('severe of punishment', i.e., severe in punishment). The definite article marks a known, defined punishment.
12.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow after, to succeed; the noun ʿiqāb refers to the consequence that follows wrongdoing: punishment

1.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
1.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

2.meaning: You (all) cut down, felled — the past-tense verb addressing a plural audience; refers literally to cutting trees or figuratively to severing something.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb, Form I, second person masculine plural. The -tum suffix marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the subject of a completed action.
2.root: ق-ط-ع (q-ṭ-ʿ) — to cut, sever, interrupt; the basic verb qaṭaʿa means to cut through

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

4.meaning: Of palm trees — specifically līna (sing. līnah) refers to a type of palm tree (some say all palms except the best variety, or soft/young palms); the genitive case here links it to the cutting.

parts.en: palm tree(s) of the lina variety

4.grammar: A feminine noun in the genitive case, indefinite (no definite article); the -in ending (tanwīn kasra) marks it as indefinite genitive, functioning as the second term of an iḍāfa or as a partitive after 'some of'.
4.root: ل-ي-ن (l-y-n) — to be soft, pliant; līna refers to a soft or particular variety of palm; the word also simply means 'palm tree'

5.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
5.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

6.meaning: You left them standing / you left them alone — the past-tense verb with an attached object pronoun -hā ('them/it', feminine).
6.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form I), second person masculine plural. The -tumū before the pronoun is the plural subject suffix with a connecting vowel; -hā is a third-person feminine singular (or feminine plural) object pronoun.
6.root: ت-ر-ك (t-r-k) — to leave, abandon, forsake, let alone

7.meaning: Standing, established, or coming to pass; that which arises or occurs. As a feminine active participle it describes the one (feminine) who/which stands or comes about.
7.grammar: An active participle ('the one standing/occurring'), made feminine by the '-a(t)' ending. The final '-an' (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a …') and in the accusative case, the form used for objects or predicates of certain verbs.

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
8.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

9.meaning: Their roots — the plural of aṣl (root, base, foundation, origin); -hā indicates 'their' (referring back to the feminine noun for trees).
9.grammar: A masculine plural noun in the genitive case; the -i ending is genitive, as the noun follows a preposition. Uṣūl is the broken plural of aṣl. The pronoun -hā refers back to the trees (feminine).
9.root: أ-ص-ل (ʾ-ṣ-l) — root, origin, foundation; the plural uṣūl means roots or foundations

10.meaning: Then by the permission / leave / sanction (of someone) — introducing that something occurred through an authorising will or grant of leave.
10.grammar: A noun preceded by two particles: 'fa-' ('then/so', linking to what precedes) and 'bi-' ('by/through', indicating means or cause). The '-i' ending on 'idhn' is genitive, required after the preposition 'bi-' and typically linking it to a following noun ('… of …').
10.root: ا-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — permission, leave, to give ear/heed

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: And that He may disgrace — the purpose clause: wa- ('and') + li- ('in order to') + yukh'ziya ('He may disgrace/humiliate'). Expresses a divine purpose in the action.
12.grammar: The lam al-taʿlīl (purposive lam) takes the following verb in the subjunctive; yukh'ziya is a Form IV verb (akhzā — to humiliate), third person masculine singular, subjunctive (the -a ending instead of -u signals subjunctive mood, required after li-).
12.root: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — to be disgraced, to disgrace; Form IV akhzā means to humiliate or bring shame upon

13.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'those who defiantly disobey', 'the rebellious', 'the morally corrupt' — people who knowingly break away from obedience to Allah and overstep the bounds of right conduct.
13.grammar: Definite plural noun (active participle in form) with the article al- ('the'). The participle stem is fāsiq, and the entire sound-plural ending -īna marks a masculine plural in the accusative or genitive case (the form used as a verb's object or after a preposition). Reconstruction: al + fāsiq + īna = al-fāsiqīna. The participle names the agent: 'those who do the act of fisq', i.e. willful disobedience.
13.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to forsake obedience, transgress, act rebelliously

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: Was restored, returned, came back — refers to spoils or wealth that returns to the community without fighting; the root conveys a returning or bringing back.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb, Form IV (afāʿa), third person masculine singular. The -a ending marks the completed past action. The hamza (glottal stop) at the beginning is the causative prefix of Form IV: fāʾa (to return) → afāʾa (to cause to return, to restore).
2.root: ف-ي-أ (f-y-ʾ) — to return; Form IV afāʾa means to cause something to return, specifically the fayʾ (spoils obtained without battle)

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

5.meaning: 'His Messenger' — a messenger or envoy, one sent with a message, here possessed by 'Him'.
5.grammar: A noun ('messenger') with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, typically signalling that the word follows a preposition or is the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …'); the pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) because of that preceding i vowel.
5.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a sending, message, messenger

6.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
6.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.
6.root: — (preposition with pronoun, no root)

7.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
7.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

8.meaning: You made an expedition, you urged forward / spurred on — refers to making horses or camels gallop swiftly; specifically used for the rapid advance of cavalry.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb, Form IV, second person masculine plural. The -tum suffix marks 'you all' as the subject. Form IV awjafa means to make an animal gallop (from Form I wajafa — to be agitated/gallop).
8.root: و-ج-ف (w-j-f) — to throb, be agitated, gallop; Form IV awjafa: to urge/drive (an animal) to gallop

9.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
9.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: Horses — the collective noun or plural for horse; khaylin specifically refers to horses as a group or as military cavalry.
11.grammar: A collective noun (or broken plural) in the genitive case, indefinite; the -in ending (tanwīn kasra) marks it as genitive indefinite, as the second term of an iḍāfa or following a preposition.
11.root: خ-ي-ل (kh-y-l) — to imagine; the noun khayl means horses (the connection is disputed; classically khayl is simply 'horses/cavalry')

12.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
12.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

13.meaning: Riding camels, she-camels — the plural of rākib or a collective noun for riding animals; specifically the camels used as riding mounts (as opposed to khaylin, horses).
13.grammar: A collective noun in the genitive case, indefinite; the -in ending (tanwīn kasra) marks it as genitive indefinite. Rikāb is the plural of rākib or an independent collective for riding camels.
13.root: ر-ك-ب (r-k-b) — to ride, to mount; rikāb (or rukub) are mounts, specifically camels used for riding

14.meaning: But, however, yet — a strong adversative particle that introduces a contrast; lākin + na (emphatic suffix) = lākinna, which governs the following noun in the accusative case.
14.grammar: Wāw is connective ('and'). Lākinna is a sister of inna — a strong particle that takes its subject in the accusative case and its predicate in the nominative (or complements via a clause). It introduces an adversative/concessive clause.
14.root: — (lākin is a particle; no triliteral root)

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
15.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

16.meaning: He gives power, He unleashes, He sets (someone) in authority over — the verb sulliṭa/yusalliṭu means to give dominion or power over something; from the root that gives sulṭān (authority/power).

parts.en: He gives power / He sets (someone) in authority over

16.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, Form II, third person masculine singular; the -u ending is indicative mood. Form II (faʿʿala) here is causative/intensive: to cause someone to have sulṭān (power/authority).
16.root: س-ل-ط (s-l-ṭ) — to have power/dominion; the noun sulṭān means authority or power; Form II yusalliṭu means to empower or give dominion

17.meaning: A noun meaning 'His messengers / His envoys' — the plural of 'messenger' (one sent with a commission) with an attached pronoun 'His.'
17.grammar: A plural noun in a possessive construction with the pronoun 'His' (-hu). The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('…disobeyed His messengers'). 'Rusul' is the broken (irregular) plural of rasūl.
17.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a sent one, messenger

18.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
18.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

19.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
19.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

20.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
20.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
20.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

21.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
21.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
21.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

22.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

23.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
23.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

24.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
24.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
24.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

25.meaning: All-powerful, fully able, ever-capable — possessing complete and effective power to do whatever is willed; one whose ability never falls short.
25.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, abiding quality ('thoroughly able'). The final -un is the indefinite nominative (nunation) — the doubled-n shows no 'the', and the -u base vowel marks the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or a predicate ('… is all-powerful').

8.meaning: 'the towns / settlements'. The plural of qarya, a town, village, or settled habitation — any gathered dwelling-place of people.
