9.meaning: Then belonging to Allah; so it is Allah's. The phrase asserts that something pertains or belongs exclusively to Allah, introduced by a connective 'then/so'.
9.grammar: A connective 'fa-' ('then/so') plus the preposition 'li-' ('to/for/belonging to') attached to the name Allah. The '-i' ending on the name is genitive, the case required after a preposition; the combination expresses ownership or entitlement: '(it is) for/belonging to Allah'.

10.meaning: And to the Messenger — the one sent (with a message). Rasūl is one dispatched bearing a communication, i.e. a messenger or envoy; with the article it denotes 'the Messenger.' The word here carries a connecting 'and,' a preposition 'to/for,' and 'the.'
10.grammar: A definite masculine noun preceded by particles. wa- is 'and,' li- is the preposition 'to/for,' and l- is 'the' (its l assimilates into the following r). The final -i is the genitive ending, required here because the noun follows the preposition 'to/for.'
10.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a messenger, an envoy

11.meaning: And for the one possessing / and to the holder of. It strings together 'and', 'for/to', and 'the possessor of' — a construction meaning 'and to him who has (something)', where what is possessed is named by the noun that follows.
11.grammar: Two prefixed particles plus a noun. wa- is 'and'; li- is 'for/to'. 'dhī' means 'owner/possessor of' and is the genitive form of the word for 'one having', its -ī ending showing that it follows the preposition li- and that a following noun will name the thing possessed ('the possessor OF …').
11.root: — (the connectors have no root; 'dhī' is a relational noun meaning 'possessor of')

12.meaning: Nearness, kinship, closeness of relation — the bond of being near in blood, hence 'relatives' or 'near kin'. The word names the quality of family closeness itself.
12.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' (the). It ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) that does not change for case; such words show their grammatical role through context rather than a changing final vowel. The sense is abstract: 'nearness of kin'.
12.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — to be near, close; nearness, kinship

13.meaning: And the orphans — children who have lost their father (and so lack support). The plural refers to such fatherless children as a group.
13.grammar: 'wa' (and) plus the definite article 'al-' (the). 'yatāmā' is a broken (irregular) plural of 'yatīm' (orphan). It ends in a fixed long -ā that stays the same regardless of grammatical case, so its role is shown by context rather than a final case vowel.

14.meaning: The poor and needy — those in straitened circumstances who lack sufficient means and are humbled by want.
14.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun meaning 'the needy', with prefixes wa- 'and' and al- 'the'. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to a noun before it ('… of …').
14.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to be still, to be subdued; one humbled by poverty

15.meaning: Son of — used in the construction 'son of the road' (ibn al-sabīl), an idiom for the traveller or wayfarer.
15.grammar: A masculine noun, 'son', with the prefix wa- 'and'. The initial alif carries a connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl): its helping vowel is not pronounced here because the preceding wa- runs straight into the word, so it reads 'wab-' in connected speech. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to the following noun in a possessive chain ('son OF …').
15.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w / b-n-y) — to build; son, offspring

16.meaning: The way, road, or path — a route one travels; very often used figuratively for a course of life, conduct, or the path of religion. The attached article makes it definite: 'the way'.
16.grammar: al- is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates to the following 's', heard as 'as-sabīl'). The final -i is the genitive ending, marking the word as joined to a preceding noun ('… OF the way') or governed by a preposition.

17.meaning: So that; in order that. A particle expressing purpose or reason, introducing the goal or aim behind an action.
17.grammar: A purpose particle (a function word, not derived from a root). It introduces the reason or goal for which something is done and typically causes the following present-tense verb to take the subjunctive mood.

18.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
18.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

19.meaning: He/it is / he comes to be. A form of the verb kāna ('to be'), linking a subject to a state or asserting that something exists or occurs.
19.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 3rd person masculine; the final -a marks the subjunctive mood, the form a verb takes after particles meaning 'so that', 'in order to', or 'that'. It expresses a state being brought about rather than a plain fact.
19.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

20.meaning: A circulation, a rotation among (people) — refers to wealth or power passing in turn among people; the sense is that goods and authority should not remain perpetually in the hands of a few.

parts.en: a circulation / rotation (of wealth or power)

20.grammar: A feminine noun in the accusative case, indefinite; the -tan ending (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as accusative indefinite. Here it functions as a predicate or an adverb of purpose: so that (wealth) does not become a dūla (i.e., rotating only among the rich).
20.root: د-و-ل (d-w-l) — to alternate, to rotate; the noun dawla/dūla refers to power or wealth circulating among people

21.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
21.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
21.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

22.meaning: The rich, the wealthy — the plural of ghanī (one who is self-sufficient, well-off, wealthy); al- makes it definite.
22.grammar: A masculine broken plural noun in the genitive case; the -i ending (with tanwīn suppressed by the definite article) is genitive, as the noun follows a preposition. Aghniyāʾ is the broken plural of ghanī.
22.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be self-sufficient, to be wealthy; ghanī means rich/independent; the plural aghniyāʾ means the wealthy

23.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
23.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
23.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

24.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
24.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

25.meaning: He gave you, He brought/delivered to you — the verb ātā in Form IV meaning 'to give, to bring'; with the pronoun -kumu addressing a plural audience.
25.grammar: A past-tense verb, Form IV (ātā/yuʾtī — to give), third person masculine singular, with a connecting vowel -u before the object pronoun. Ātā is a defective root (final weak letter); the past tense shows the contracted form. -Kumu is the second-person masculine plural object pronoun.
25.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, to bring; Form IV āta/yuʾtī means to give, to bestow

26.meaning: 'The Messenger' — one sent with a message; in religious usage, a prophet commissioned by Allah to deliver revelation to people.
26.grammar: 'al-' is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following r, doubling it). 'rasūl' is a noun meaning 'one who is sent, an envoy/messenger'. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or a word simply being named.

27.meaning: So take it, so accept it — the imperative with the fa- of consequence: 'then take/receive it'.
27.grammar: Fa- indicates a result or command following from what came before. Khudhū is the Form I imperative, second person masculine plural (the basic imperative of akhadha — to take). The -hu is the third-person masculine singular object pronoun.
27.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, accept; the imperative khudh (singular) / khudhū (plural) means 'take!'

28.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
28.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

29.meaning: He forbade you, he prohibited you from — the verb nahā means to forbid or prohibit; with the pronoun -kum addressing the second-person plural.
29.grammar: A past-tense verb, Form I, third person masculine singular, with a weak final letter (the alif maqṣūra represents the weak root letter). The -kum is the second-person masculine plural object pronoun.
29.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to forbid, prohibit, prevent; the verb nahā means to forbid or restrain; the noun nahy means prohibition

30.meaning: A combination meaning 'from him / from it / about him.' The preposition denotes moving away from, departing from, or concerning a thing, and the pronoun refers to a single masculine entity.
30.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. ʿan governs the genitive and conveys separation or 'concerning.' The attached -hu marks a third-person masculine singular object ('him/it').

31.meaning: So refrain, so hold back, desist — the Form VIII imperative of intahā (to come to an end, to desist from); fa- connects it to the preceding prohibition.
31.grammar: Fa- marks a consequential command. Intahū is the Form VIII imperative, second person masculine plural. Form VIII (Form I root: nahā) gives intahā — to come to the end of, to refrain from. The -ū is the masculine plural imperative suffix.
31.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to forbid; Form VIII intahā means to refrain, to come to a stop, to desist

32.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'guard yourselves / be mindful and on your guard.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself by being conscious of Allah and shielding oneself from wrongdoing and its consequences.
32.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you (all).' The -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressees ('you all'). The pattern (form VIII, from waqā 'to protect') gives the sense of taking protective care for oneself.
32.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

33.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
33.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

34.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
34.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

35.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
35.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

36.meaning: Severe, intense, harsh, or mighty — describing something powerful and unsparing in its degree.
36.grammar: An adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('severe, intense'). The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as a subject or predicate.
36.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, severe

37.meaning: The punishment, penalty, or retribution; a consequence imposed in requital for wrongdoing.
37.grammar: A definite noun with prefixed al- ("the"). The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… of …") or follows a preposition.
37.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow/come after; consequence, punishment

1.meaning: For the poor / to the needy — a preposition 'for' joined to 'the poor,' the destitute who lack sufficient means; the plural of one in a state of poverty and need.
1.grammar: The preposition li- ('for') merged with the definite article al- (here written 'lil-'), on the plural noun 'the poor.' The preposition forces the genitive case, shown by the final -i; the genitive is the case taken after a preposition. The noun is a broken (irregular) plural meaning 'poor/needy people.'
1.root: ف-ق-ر (f-q-r) — poverty, need, to be poor

2.meaning: 'The emigrants / those who migrated' — those who forsook their homes and migrated for the sake of their faith, leaving one place and people for another. The form names those who undertake such a departure.
2.grammar: An active participle of the form-III stem ('one who migrates / parts from'), made definite by al- ('the') and put in the sound masculine plural. The -īna ending is the masculine-plural form used in the accusative (object) or genitive (after a preposition or in a possessive phrase) — distinct from the subject form -ūna; the -ī- carries the plural and the -na marks this case.
2.root: ه-ج-ر (h-j-r) — to forsake, depart, emigrate

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: They were expelled, they were driven out — the passive past-tense verb; refers to being forced to leave one's home.
4.grammar: A passive past-tense verb (Form IV passive), third person masculine plural. The -ū suffix marks masculine plural subject. The passive is formed by changing the vowel pattern: active akhraja → passive ukhrija. The -ū shortens before the final vowel in passive plural.
4.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit; Form IV akhraja means to expel/drive out; the passive ukhrija means 'they were expelled'

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: Their homes or dwellings; the places where they live. 'Diyār' is the plural of 'dār,' a house, abode, or region one inhabits.
6.grammar: A plural noun followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The -i vowel on the stem is the genitive case, here triggered by the attached possessor and typical after prepositions or in possessive linkage ('the homes of…').
6.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn/encircle; dwelling, abode

7.meaning: And their properties, and their wealth — amwāl is the plural of māl (property, wealth, possessions); wa- connects it to the preceding noun.
7.grammar: Wāw is connective. Amwāl is a masculine broken plural noun in the genitive case; the -i ending (with -him) is genitive, as the noun is in a genitive construct or follows a preposition. The suffix -him is the third-person masculine plural possessive.
7.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — to have property; the noun māl means wealth or property; its plural amwāl covers all forms of possessions

8.meaning: 'they seek / pursue / strive after' — a group actively looking for and aiming to obtain something, whether a material gain or a spiritual reward. It conveys ongoing endeavour and quest.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb of the reflexive Form VIII. The 'ya-' prefix plus the -ūna ending together mean 'they (masculine) seek'. The retained 'na' marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('they do seek'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by certain particles.
8.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive for

9.meaning: Bounty, grace, favour, or abundance; something good given freely and beyond what is owed. It can mean material provision (such as profit from trade) or divine grace and excess generosity.
9.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -an (accusative case with nunation) typically marks it as the direct object of a verb ('seeking a bounty') or as the goal of an action. The nunation also makes it indefinite ('a bounty / some favour').
9.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to be in excess, to surpass; hence grace, bounty, superiority

10.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
10.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: 'and good pleasure / approval' — Allah's gracious acceptance and favour; the contented approval of one party toward another. Riḍwān is an intensive form denoting full, abundant pleasure and goodwill.
12.grammar: A noun joined by 'wa' ('and'). The -an ending is accusative with the 'n' sound (nunation) marking it indefinite — the form a noun takes as a direct object: 'and (seeking) good pleasure'.
12.root: ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-y) — to be pleased, content; to approve and accept

13.meaning: And (they are) helping — the present-tense verb yanṣurūna with wāw ('and') prefixed; refers to ongoing mutual support or assistance.

parts.en: they help / they support / they give victory to

13.grammar: Wāw is connective. Yanṣurūna is a Form I present/imperfect verb, third person masculine plural; the -ūna ending marks masculine plural indicative. The root naṣara means to help or give victory.
13.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, support, give victory; the noun naṣr means victory; the verb naṣara means to aid

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
14.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

15.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
15.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.

16.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
16.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

17.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
17.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

18.meaning: The truthful ones, the sincere ones — the plural active participle of ṣadaqa (to be true/sincere); refers to those who are genuinely faithful in word and deed.
18.grammar: A masculine sound plural noun in the nominative case; the -ūna ending marks nominative (as opposed to accusative/genitive -īna). The definite article makes it 'the truthful ones'. This is the active participle (ṣādiq) in its plural form.
18.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — to be true, truthful, sincere; the active participle ṣādiq means truthful; the plural ṣādiqūn means the sincere/truthful ones

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: They settled, they took up residence — the Form V verb tabawwaʾa means to take a place as one's abode, to settle in; refers to the Anṣār who settled Medina before the emigrants arrived.

parts.en: they settled / they took up abode

2.grammar: A past-tense verb, Form V (tabawwaʾa), third person masculine plural. The -ū suffix marks plural masculine. Form V here means to take something (a place, a home) for oneself, reflexively.
2.root: ب-و-أ (b-w-ʾ) — to return to a place, to settle; Form V tabawwaʾa means to take a dwelling for oneself, to settle down

3.meaning: The home, the abode — al-dār is a feminine noun meaning the house, home, abode, or realm; here likely referring to Medina as the abode/home of faith.
3.grammar: A feminine noun in the accusative case; the -a ending is accusative, as dār is the object of the verb tabawwaʾū ('they settled in the home'). The definite article makes it 'the (specific) home'.
3.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to go around; the noun dār (pl. diyār) refers to a dwelling place, home, or realm

4.meaning: And (accepted) the faith — al-īmān refers to faith, belief, the act of believing; here it is paired with 'the home' in referring to what the Anṣār embraced before the Muhājirūn arrived.
4.grammar: Wāw is connective. Al-īmān is a masculine verbal noun (maṣdar) in the accusative case; the -a ending is accusative, parallel to al-dāra. The definite article makes it 'the faith' (i.e., Islam/faith as a specific concept).
4.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to believe; the maṣdar (verbal noun) īmān means faith, belief, trust

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
6.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
6.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

7.meaning: They love — the present-tense verb yuḥibbūna expressing ongoing affection or love; the Form IV root means to love.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, Form IV (aḥabba), third person masculine plural; the -ūna ending marks indicative masculine plural. The tashdīd on the bāʾ reflects the double-letter root.
7.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — to love; Form IV aḥabba/yuḥibbu means to love; the noun ḥubb means love

8.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
8.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

9.meaning: He emigrated, he migrated — the Form III verb hājara conveys the mutual/reciprocal sense of migration (migrating from one party to another); specifically refers to the hijra (emigration from Mecca to Medina).
9.grammar: A past-tense verb, Form III (fāʿala), third person masculine singular. The -a ending marks completed past action. Form III here implies a migration 'toward' or 'from' someone/somewhere, highlighting the relational nature of the emigration.
9.root: ه-ج-ر (h-j-r) — to abandon, emigrate; Form III hājara specifically refers to the act of hijra (emigration)

10.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
10.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
10.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: 'they find' — to come upon, obtain, or encounter something; to perceive a thing to be present or available.
12.grammar: A present/future verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they …'). The ending -ūna combines the plural 'they' (-ū) with the indicative marker -na, signalling a simple ongoing or future statement (not negated or subjunctive). The ya- prefix marks the third person.
12.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon, obtain

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: Their breasts / their chests — the bosoms of a group of males, the chest regarded as the seat of feelings and inner thoughts, with an attached 'their'.
14.grammar: A plural noun ('breasts') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their', referring to a group of males). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive ending, signalling that the noun follows a preposition or is the possessed term in a possessive phrase.

15.meaning: A need, want, or requirement — something one has need of, or a matter one wishes to fulfil.
15.grammar: A feminine noun (the -ah ending becomes -t- before the case vowel). The -an ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a need') and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the object of a verb or, as often, to express a reason or circumstance ('out of a need').

16.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
16.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

17.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
17.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
17.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

18.meaning: But they prefer (others over themselves) — the Form II verb āthara (yūthiru) means to give preference to; here with wāw ('and/but') introducing the clause of selfless generosity.

parts.en: they prefer / they give precedence (to others)

18.grammar: Wāw is connective/adversative. Yuʾthirūna is a Form IV present/imperfect verb, third person masculine plural; the -ūna ending marks indicative. Form IV āthara means to prefer someone/something over oneself.
18.root: أ-ث-ر (ʾ-th-r) — to leave a trace, to prefer; Form IV āthara/yuʾthiru means to give precedence or preference to someone else

19.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
19.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

20.meaning: Themselves / their own selves — the noun nafs ('self, soul, person, inner being') joined to a pronoun 'their'. Used reflexively it means 'their own selves' and conveys the inmost self, the seat of desires and the person as a whole.
20.grammar: The plural noun anfus ('selves') carries the genitive -i ending followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by a preposition or joined to a preceding word; -him makes it 'their selves'.
20.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

21.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
21.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

22.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

22.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

23.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
23.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

24.meaning: Poverty, destitution, need — the noun khaṣāṣa refers to a gap or deficiency, by extension poverty or privation; describes a state of lack or want.
24.grammar: A feminine noun in the nominative case, indefinite; the -tun ending (tanwīn ḍamma) marks it as nominative indefinite. Here it functions as the subject of a clause ('even though poverty is with them').
24.root: خ-ص-ص (kh-ṣ-ṣ) — to be specific, to have a gap; the noun khaṣāṣa refers to a gap or deficiency, hence poverty or need

25.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
25.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

26.meaning: He/one is saved, protected — the passive imperfect of waqā (to protect, to shield); the Form I passive indicates 'being protected'.

parts.en: he is saved / he is protected (from)

26.grammar: A passive present/imperfect verb, Form I, third person masculine singular; the -a ending signals the subjunctive mood, triggered by the preceding man ('whoever') in a conditional clause. The passive vowel pattern (u + o on the middle radical) marks it as passive.
26.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to protect, guard, shield; the passive yūqā means 'to be protected/saved from'

27.meaning: Stinginess, miserliness, avarice — the noun shuḥḥ refers to extreme miserliness or greed; it combines stinginess with a deep inner reluctance to spend or give.
27.grammar: A masculine noun in the accusative case, definite (governed by wiqāya/protection from 'the' stinginess implied). The -a ending here is accusative following the preposition or as the direct object of the passive saving.
27.root: ش-ح-ح (sh-ḥ-ḥ) — to be stingy, miserly; the noun shuḥḥ means extreme miserliness or greed with an inner aversion to giving

28.meaning: 'Himself; his own self/soul' — the inner self, soul, or person of a male individual; used reflexively to point back to the person himself.
28.grammar: The noun 'nafs' ('self/soul') with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically follows a preposition or links the noun possessively to what precedes ('the self OF him' = 'himself'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this preceding '-i' vowel; the long vowel mark indicates it is pronounced '-hī'.

29.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
29.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

30.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
30.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

31.meaning: 'The successful / the ones who flourish' — those who attain what they seek and are saved from what they fear. The underlying sense is of prospering, thriving, and winning through to lasting wellbeing and salvation, not merely worldly success.
31.grammar: A definite active participle (Form IV) in the masculine plural: 'the ones who succeed/prosper'. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate identifying who someone is.

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: They came — the act of coming or arriving, attributed to a group ('they').
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix '-ū' marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), denoting a completed act of arriving carried out by a group.
2.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: "after them / following them" — the noun baʿd ('after, afterward') with the attached pronoun 'them', denoting what comes later in time than a group.
4.grammar: A time-noun used like a preposition, with an attached pronoun. The -i ending is genitive, the form taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive link. The suffix -him means 'them' (its vowel is -hi- to harmonise with the preceding -i).

5.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

6.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

6.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

7.meaning: Forgive! — a plea or command to pardon, to cover over and blot out wrongdoing. It carries the sense of veiling a fault so it is no longer held against the offender.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person: 'forgive!'. The vowelless final -r reflects the imperative form. It is commonly followed by 'us' or 'for me' to specify whom to pardon.
7.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and pardon; mercy that blots out sin

8.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
8.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

9.meaning: And for our brothers — the preposition li- ('for/to') + ikhwān ('brothers') + nā ('our'). Expresses a supplication or wish on behalf of one's brothers in faith.
9.grammar: Wāw is connective. Li- is a preposition of benefit ('for'). Ikhwāni is a masculine broken plural noun in the genitive case (governed by li-); the -i ending is genitive. The -nā suffix is the first-person plural possessive pronoun ('our').
9.root: أ-خ-و (ʾ-kh-w) — brother; the plural ikhwān means brothers (in faith or lineage)

10.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
10.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

11.meaning: They preceded us — the past-tense verb sabaqūnā: they went ahead of us, they came before us in something (here, in faith).
11.grammar: A past-tense verb, Form I, third person masculine plural. The -ū marks the masculine plural subject. The -nā is the first-person plural object pronoun ('us').
11.root: س-ب-ق (s-b-q) — to precede, to go ahead, to outstrip; the verb sabaqa means to come before or to surpass

12.meaning: With/by means of faith — that is, the inward belief and trust in Allah, His messengers, and the unseen truths He has revealed; an active conviction of the heart that issues in commitment and action. The attached preposition adds the sense 'with' or 'by means of'.
12.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with' or 'by means of'; al- is the definite article 'the'. The final -i is the genitive ending, which here is required because the noun follows the preposition bi-: prepositions force the following noun into the genitive.
12.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to believe

13.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

14.meaning: You make, you set up, you render/turn (one thing into another) — to place, appoint, or cause something to become a certain way.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single masculine 'you' (the ta- prefix). Its vowel-less ending (jussive mood) is the form used after particles like 'do not' (a command or prohibition) or 'if'; it does not stand as a plain statement on its own.
14.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, appoint, render

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: Our hearts — qulūb is the plural of qalb (heart); -nā marks possession ('our'). The heart in Quranic usage is the seat of understanding, faith, and moral character.
16.grammar: A masculine broken plural noun in the genitive case; the -i ending is genitive, as the noun follows a preposition or is in a genitive construct. The suffix -nā is the first-person plural possessive.
16.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over, to flip; the noun qalb (heart) refers to the organ that 'turns' — the seat of thought, emotion, and faith

17.meaning: Any rancor, any grudge, any ill-will — the noun ghillan refers to a hidden resentment or malice lodged in the heart; from the root meaning to be obscured or covered.
17.grammar: A masculine noun in the accusative case, indefinite; the -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as accusative indefinite. Here it is the object of lā tajaʿal ('do not place'): 'do not place any rancor in our hearts'.
17.root: غ-ل-ل (gh-l-l) — to be hidden, to filter through; the noun ghillan (or ghilll) refers to hidden malice, grudge, or resentment

18.meaning: 'For/to those who …' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the masculine plural relative pronoun 'those who,' which introduces a description of a group by something they do.
18.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to') fused with the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). Relative pronouns like this do not change for case; they point ahead to a clause that describes the group ('those who …').

19.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
19.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

20.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

20.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
20.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

21.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
21.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

22.meaning: Most kind, gentle, and compassionate; one who is full of tender pity and gentleness. Raʾūf is an intensive form stressing deep, abundant kindness — a name/attribute of Allah meaning 'the Ever-Gentle, Most Compassionate.'

parts.en: full of kindness / most gentle (the final -un is the nominative ending with tanwīn, marking an indefinite predicate)

22.grammar: An intensive adjective ('one full of …') describing abundant kindness. The final '-un' is the nominative case ending together with tanwīn (the '-n' that marks an indefinite noun): it typically marks the word as a subject or, as here, a predicate/description ('… is most kind'). The intensive pattern stresses depth and constancy of the quality.

23.meaning: Most Merciful / ever-compassionate — one whose mercy is deep, constant, and abundantly bestowed; an intensive form stressing enduring tenderness and care. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
23.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a lasting, abundant quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is most merciful").

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: They acted as hypocrites — they professed faith outwardly while concealing disbelief or ill intent inwardly; they were two-faced in religion.

parts.en: they played the hypocrite (Form III stem)

5.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form III. The '-ū' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they did'). It denotes the completed act of behaving hypocritically — showing one thing while hiding another.
5.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — hypocrisy; a burrow with two exits (the image behind 'nifāq')

6.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
6.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'
6.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — speech; saying, uttering, asserting

7.meaning: To their brothers — the preposition li- ('to/for') + ikhwān ('brothers') + him ('their'). Refers to false support given to others.
7.grammar: Li- is a preposition; ikhwāni is a masculine broken plural in the genitive case (governed by the preposition); the suffix -himu is the third-person masculine plural possessive pronoun ('their'), with a connecting vowel -u.
7.root: أ-خ-و (ʾ-kh-w) — brother; the plural ikhwān refers to brothers by faith or blood

8.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
8.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

9.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: People of / folk of / those belonging to — the family, followers, or possessors of something (as in 'people of the Book'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with a thing.
11.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/folk of'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('people OF …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.
11.root: ء-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, people belonging to

12.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
12.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

13.meaning: An emphatic conditional opener combining an oath-like emphasis with 'if' — roughly 'most certainly, if (such-and-such happens)…', strongly stressing the condition and the response that follows.
13.grammar: Two particles fused together: an emphatic la- that signals a coming oath or strong assertion, plus in ('if') introducing a condition. Together they set up an emphatic 'if… then surely…' construction. Neither has a case ending; particles do not inflect.

14.meaning: You are expelled, you are driven out — the passive past-tense verb, second person masculine plural; addresses those who were forced to leave their homes.
14.grammar: A passive past-tense verb (Form IV passive), second person masculine plural. The passive vowel shift (active form: akhraja → passive: ukhrija) combined with the -tum suffix marks 'you all were expelled'.
14.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out; Form IV akhraja means to expel/eject; its passive means 'to be expelled'

15.meaning: Surely we will leave / we will certainly go out — the emphatic form with lam- (assertive prefix) + nayn of emphasis (nūn al-tawkīd): 'we will definitely go out'.

parts.en: we will go out / we will leave

15.grammar: The lam al-tawkīd (assertive lam) combines with the heavy nūn al-tawkīd (-anna at the end) to give the strongest form of emphasis: 'we most certainly will leave.' Nakhrujanna is a Form I present/imperfect verb, first person plural, with the emphatic nūn.
15.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit; the verb kharaja means to go out; here in the emphatic future: 'we will absolutely leave'

16.meaning: An expression meaning 'with you' — combining the word for accompaniment, togetherness, or presence-alongside with the attached pronoun 'you' (a group). It signals being in the company of, or on the side of, the addressed people.
16.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment (maʿa, 'with/in the company of') carrying the attached pronoun -kum ('you,' for a group of males). It expresses togetherness or being alongside the people addressed.

17.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
17.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

18.meaning: We will obey — the present/imperfect verb nuṭīʿu expresses future intention or current disposition to obey; from Form IV of ṭāʿa (to obey).
18.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, Form IV (aṭāʿa — to obey), first person plural; the -u ending marks indicative mood. Form IV aṭāʿa/yuṭīʿu means to obey or comply.
18.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, to be submissive; Form IV aṭāʿa/nuṭīʿu means to obey or be compliant

19.meaning: Among you / in you: locates something within a group of people addressed in the plural.
19.grammar: A preposition 'in/among' with an attached pronoun -kum meaning 'you' for a group of males (or mixed group). Words after the preposition fī stand in the genitive, which is why the pronoun takes this object form. The whole expresses presence or location within the addressed group.

20.meaning: Anyone / a single one: 'one' used to mean a sole individual, especially in negative or conditional contexts ('not anyone', 'any single person').
20.grammar: A noun meaning 'one / a single one', frequently used for 'anyone' when paired with a negation. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case typically used for a verb's object.

21.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
21.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.

22.meaning: and if; but if. It combines a connective 'and/but' with a conditional particle that introduces a hypothetical or possible case ('if such-and-such happens…').
22.grammar: Two particles joined: the connector 'wa' ('and/but') and 'in' ('if'). 'In' introduces a condition and typically puts the verb that follows into the jussive mood, setting up an 'if … then …' relationship. Neither particle takes a case ending.

23.meaning: You are fought, you are attacked — the passive past-tense verb, second person masculine plural; used in a conditional context ('if you are fought/attacked').

parts.en: you (pl.) were fought / you were attacked

23.grammar: A passive past-tense verb, Form III passive (qātala → passive qūtila), second person masculine plural. The passive pattern (ū on the first syllable, i on the second) combined with the -tum suffix marks 'you all were fought/attacked'.
23.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill; Form III qātala means to fight (mutually); its passive qūtila means 'to be fought against'

24.meaning: Certainly we will help you — the emphatic form lam + verb + nūn al-tawkīd + object pronoun: the strongest assurance of help.

parts.en: we will help / we will support

24.grammar: The assertive lam + the heavy nūn al-tawkīd (-anna) create emphatic emphasis. Nanṣuranna is Form I, first person plural, with the emphatic nūn. The -kum is the second-person masculine plural object pronoun.
24.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, support, give victory; the verb naṣara means to aid; the emphatic future form promises definite assistance

25.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
25.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
25.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

26.meaning: 'he bears witness / testifies' — to give firm testimony, to attest to the truth of something with certain knowledge.
26.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix means 'he' (the doer), and the -u ending marks the ordinary, unrestricted present tense ('he bears witness / does testify').
26.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

27.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
27.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

28.meaning: "Surely liars / ones who lie." The plural noun "liars" (those who speak falsehood), fronted by an emphatic "la-" meaning "surely / indeed."
28.grammar: An active-participle noun, masculine plural, meaning "ones who lie." The "-ūna" ending is the sound-masculine-plural in the nominative — the case used for a subject or for the completing word of a sentence ("they are …"). The emphatic la- ("surely") often pairs with the affirming particle inna.

1.meaning: An emphatic conditional opener combining an oath-like emphasis with 'if' — roughly 'most certainly, if (such-and-such happens)…', strongly stressing the condition and the response that follows.
1.grammar: Two particles fused together: an emphatic la- that signals a coming oath or strong assertion, plus in ('if') introducing a condition. Together they set up an emphatic 'if… then surely…' construction. Neither has a case ending; particles do not inflect.

2.meaning: They were expelled, they were driven out — the passive past-tense verb; refers to being forced to leave one's home.
2.grammar: A passive past-tense verb (Form IV passive), third person masculine plural. The -ū suffix marks masculine plural subject. The passive is formed by changing the vowel pattern: active akhraja → passive ukhrija. The -ū shortens before the final vowel in passive plural.
2.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit; Form IV akhraja means to expel/drive out; the passive ukhrija means 'they were expelled'

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: They will go out, they will leave — the present/imperfect verb expressing future action; third person masculine plural.

parts.en: they go out / they will leave

4.grammar: A Form I present/imperfect verb, third person masculine plural; the -ūna ending marks indicative masculine plural. In context (a condition or reported speech), it may carry a future meaning: 'they will leave'.
4.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit; the present/future form yakhrujūna means 'they (will) go out'

5.meaning: With them, in their company or possession — expressing accompaniment or togetherness. Maʿa denotes being alongside or in the presence of someone or something.
5.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment ('with') fixed in the -a form, joined to the pronoun -hum ('them'). Together they express that something is in the company or possession of a group.

6.meaning: A combination meaning 'and surely if' — introducing a hypothetical condition ('if…') sworn by an implied oath, so that the outcome is strongly anticipated; roughly 'and by all means, if…'.
6.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case ending: wa- 'and', the lam al-qasam (the 'lam of swearing') that marks the following condition as sworn by an implied oath, and in 'if' which sets up the condition. This oath-lam construction correlates with a later response clause that itself carries emphasis (an emphatic lam plus the 'nūn of emphasis' on its verb), giving the sense 'and [I swear] if … they would surely …'.

7.meaning: They are fought — the passive past-tense verb, third person masculine plural; refers to being attacked or fought against.

parts.en: they were fought / they were attacked

7.grammar: A passive past-tense verb, Form III passive, third person masculine plural. The passive pattern (ū, i) + the -ū suffix for masculine plural past marks 'they were fought'.
7.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill; Form III passive qūtilū means 'they were fought against'

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: They will help them — the present/imperfect verb of naṣara with an attached object pronoun -nahum ('them'); third person masculine plural.
9.grammar: A Form I present/imperfect verb, third person masculine plural; the -ūna ending is indicative. The object pronoun -hum (masculine plural) indicates 'them' as the recipients of the help. Together yanṣurūnahum means 'they help them'.
9.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, support, give victory; yanṣurūnahum means 'they support them'

10.meaning: A combination meaning 'and surely if' — introducing a hypothetical condition ('if…') sworn by an implied oath, so that the outcome is strongly anticipated; roughly 'and by all means, if…'.
10.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case ending: wa- 'and', the lam al-qasam (the 'lam of swearing') that marks the following condition as sworn by an implied oath, and in 'if' which sets up the condition. This oath-lam construction correlates with a later response clause that itself carries emphasis (an emphatic lam plus the 'nūn of emphasis' on its verb), giving the sense 'and [I swear] if … they would surely …'.

11.meaning: They helped them — the past-tense verb naṣara in third person masculine plural with an object pronoun.
11.grammar: A Form I past-tense verb, third person masculine plural (-ū suffix). The -hum is the third-person masculine plural object pronoun. Naṣarūhum means 'they aided/helped them'.
11.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, support, give victory; the past tense naṣarū + hum = 'they helped them'

12.meaning: They will certainly turn (away/back) — the emphatic lam + yuwallu + nūn al-tawkīd: an emphatic assertion that they will turn their backs or flee.

parts.en: they will turn (their backs) / they will flee

12.grammar: The assertive lam + heavy nūn al-tawkīd create emphatic certainty. Yuwallunna is Form II present/imperfect, third person masculine plural, with the emphatic nūn; Form II wallā/yuwallī means to cause to turn, or to turn (intransitively: to flee, to retreat).
12.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near, to turn to; Form II wallā/yuwallī means to turn (someone) away; used idiomatically for fleeing (turning one's back)

13.meaning: 'The backs' — the plural of 'back' (the rear of a person or body), commonly evoking the act of turning one's back, retreating, or fleeing.
13.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a ending is accusative, the case that commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
13.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — back, rear; that which comes behind

14.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
14.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

15.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
15.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

16.meaning: To be helped, aided, or given victory — for support to be granted, especially against an adversary.
16.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, masculine plural 'they.' The yu- prefix is the third-person masculine imperfect marker; the passive sense ('they are being helped,' by an unnamed helper) comes from the internal vowelling rather than from the prefix itself. The -ūna ending marks a plural subject in the plain (indicative) present, used for an ongoing or general fact.
16.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, grant victory

1.meaning: Certainly you — the emphatic la- + antum: 'verily you (all)' or 'indeed you'. The la- is an assertive particle affirming the following statement.
1.grammar: La- is the assertive lam (lam al-ibtidāʾ or lam al-tawkīd), emphasizing the sentence. Antum is the detached second-person masculine plural pronoun, functioning as the subject of the following predicate.
1.root: — (la- is a particle; antum is a pronoun; no root)

2.meaning: 'Harder / more intense / stronger.' A comparative meaning something is greater in hardness, severity, force, or intensity than what it is compared with; the base sense is being firm, severe, and strong.
2.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective ('more severe / harder'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject or as the descriptive predicate of the subject. Built on the 'afʿal' pattern used for comparisons ('more …').
2.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be firm, intense, severe, strong

3.meaning: (In) fear, dread, awe — the noun rahba (or rahbatan) refers to a feeling of fear or reverential awe; here it indicates the fear felt toward the believers.
3.grammar: A feminine noun in the accusative case, indefinite; the -tan ending (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as accusative indefinite. Here it functions as a circumstantial accusative or as the object of a verbal idea: 'they have more fear of you'.
3.root: ر-ه-ب (r-h-b) — to fear, to be in awe; the noun rahba means fear or reverential awe; the verb rahiba means to fear

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: Their breasts / their chests — the bosoms of a group of males, the chest regarded as the seat of feelings and inner thoughts, with an attached 'their'.
5.grammar: A plural noun ('breasts') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their', referring to a group of males). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive ending, signalling that the noun follows a preposition or is the possessed term in a possessive phrase.

6.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
6.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
8.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

9.meaning: A connector meaning 'because they…' or 'by reason that they…'. It fuses the preposition bi- (here giving a cause, 'because of') with anna ('that', an emphatic particle introducing a fact) and the attached pronoun -hum ('they').
9.grammar: bi- here gives a causal sense ('because of'). anna is an emphatic particle meaning 'that' which introduces a statement of fact and takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; the attached -hum is that pronoun, a masculine plural 'they'. Together they give a reason: 'because they …'.

10.meaning: 'A people / folk / community' — a group of people bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared identity.
10.grammar: An indefinite collective noun ('a people'), grammatically singular but referring to a group. The -un ending is indefinite ('a') and nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
10.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a group that stands together

11.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
11.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

12.meaning: Verb meaning 'they understand / comprehend deeply' — to grasp the inner meaning of something with discernment, a perceptive, penetrating understanding.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb, masculine third-person plural. The complete '-ūna' ending (with the 'nūn' intact) signals the indicative mood — a plain ongoing statement, 'they understand.' The root connotes deep, discerning comprehension rather than mere hearing.
12.root: ف-ق-ه (f-q-h) — to understand deeply, comprehend with insight (source of the word fiqh)

2.meaning: They fight you / they wage war against you. A present-tense verb of mutual combat with an object pronoun 'you (plural).'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the third (mutual) pattern, third-person masculine plural ('they…'). The yu- prefix (vowelled with a ḍamma, as the third pattern requires) signals a 'they' subject, and the -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the indicative (a stated, ongoing action). The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you all.'
2.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill; in this pattern, to fight, do battle

3.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
3.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

4.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
4.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
