5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: Towns, villages, settlements — the plural of qarya (a village, town, settlement); used broadly for inhabited places.
6.grammar: A feminine broken plural noun in the accusative or genitive case, indefinite; the -an ending here reflects the accusative indefinite (tanwīn fatḥa) of a defective noun (ending in alif maqṣūra). Quran is the broken plural of qarya.
6.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — to be hospitable, to settle; the noun qarya means a village or settlement; its plural quran covers towns and settlements

7.meaning: Fortified, strongly built — the passive participle of ḥaṣṣana (Form II: to fortify); describes towns or places that have been made impregnable.
7.grammar: A feminine passive participle (Form II: muḥaṣṣan), in the genitive case indefinite; the -atin ending (tanwīn kasra) marks it genitive indefinite, agreeing with the feminine noun it modifies (quran — towns). The passivity indicates these towns were made fortified.
7.root: ح-ص-ن (ḥ-ṣ-n) — to fortify; Form II ḥaṣṣana means to make impregnable; the passive participle muḥaṣṣan means fortified

8.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
8.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: Behind, beyond, or after — a noun of place/sequence pointing to what lies past or following something. It can mean 'behind' in space or 'after / beyond' in time or order.
10.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. This is a place-noun functioning adverbially. The -i ending is genitive: it links the word to a following noun in an 'of / behind …' relationship or follows a preposition.
10.root: و-ر-ي / و-ر-ء (w-r-y) — being behind or to the rear

11.meaning: Walls — the plural of jidar (a wall); refers to the fortification walls of settlements or strongholds.
11.grammar: A masculine broken plural noun in the genitive case, indefinite; the -in ending (tanwīn kasra) marks it genitive indefinite. Judur is the broken plural of jidar (wall). Here it follows a preposition or is in a genitive chain.
11.root: ج-د-ر (j-d-r) — to be appropriate, to build a wall; the noun jidar means a wall; its plural judur means walls

12.meaning: Their violence, their strength, their power in battle — bas refers to strength, valor in war, or the ability to cause harm; -hum marks possession ('their').
12.grammar: A masculine noun in the nominative case; the -u ending marks it as the subject (nominative) of the clause. The suffix -hum is the third-person masculine plural possessive.
12.root: ب-أ-س (b-ʾ-s) — to be brave, to have strength/might; the noun bas means strength, valor, or intensity of force

13.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
13.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
13.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

14.meaning: Severe, intense, harsh, or mighty in force. Describes something powerful and unrelenting in its strength or rigor.
14.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting a firmly established quality (intensity, severity). The final -un ending combines the nominative case (used for the subject or a predicate describing who/what something is) with nunation (the -n sound), which marks the word as indefinite, i.e. 'a severe one' rather than 'the severe one'.
14.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, firm, severe

15.meaning: You think they (are united) / you consider them — the present verb of ḥasiba (to think, to consider, to suppose); with the object pronoun -hum ('them').

parts.en: you think / you suppose / you consider

15.grammar: A Form I present/imperfect verb, second person masculine singular; the -u ending marks indicative mood. The -hum is the third-person masculine plural object pronoun.
15.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to count, reckon, think; the verb ḥasiba/yaḥsibu means to suppose or think (something about someone)

16.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.

17.meaning: But their hearts — wāw + qulūb ('hearts') + -hum ('their'): introduces a contrast ('but their hearts are divided').
17.grammar: Wāw is connective/adversative ('but'). Qulūb is a masculine broken plural noun in the nominative case; the -u ending marks it as the subject (nominative) of the following clause. The suffix -hum is third-person masculine plural possessive.
17.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn, flip; the noun qalb (heart) refers to the seat of consciousness and faith; its plural qulūb means hearts

18.meaning: 'Diverse' / 'various' / 'of different kinds' — describing things that are scattered in variety, assorted, differing one from another.
18.grammar: An adjective in a plural pattern meaning 'of many different sorts'. It ends in a fixed long -ā and does not change for case. It characterises a group as varied and assorted. The root conveys dispersal and difference.

21.grammar: An indefinite collective noun ('a people'), grammatically singular but referring to a group. The -un ending is indefinite ('a') and nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
21.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a group that stands together

22.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
22.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

23.meaning: 'They understand / use reason.' To comprehend, reason, and grasp things with the intellect — to 'tie down' meaning with the mind, to think rationally and exercise sound judgment.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame means 'they [do]' for a group of males or a mixed group. The full -ūna ending (with the final -na intact) marks the indicative mood, i.e. a plain factual statement. The root sense is binding/restraining, hence using the mind to 'hold' meaning.
23.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to bind, restrain; intellect, reason

1.meaning: An expression meaning 'like the likeness of' or 'as the example of.' It joins the comparison word 'ka' (like, as) to the noun for a likeness/parable, setting up a comparison: 'comparable to the case of…'
1.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like, as') prefixed to a noun. Because ka- functions like a preposition, the noun takes the -i genitive ending, the case used after prepositions and to link 'the likeness OF …' to a following noun.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
4.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
4.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

5.meaning: An adjective meaning 'near, close, close at hand' — describing something short in distance, time, or relationship, easily reached or soon to come.
5.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern ('near, close'). The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (nunation), which typically marks the word as agreeing with an accusative noun it describes, or otherwise governed into the accusative; the tanwīn shows it is indefinite.

6.meaning: They tasted; they experienced something directly and personally. Beyond literal tasting with the tongue, it commonly means to undergo and feel the full impact of something, such as a punishment or a consequence.
6.grammar: A past-tense (completed action) verb with the '-ū' ending marking a third-person masculine plural subject: 'they (men/people) tasted'. The action is presented as already done.
6.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste, to experience

7.meaning: Grievous consequence, ruinous outcome, or the bitter penalty of an action — the harmful aftermath that an evil deed brings upon its doer.
7.grammar: A singular noun preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The -a ending marks the accusative case (often the direct object); on a noun lacking tanwīn it commonly indicates a construct, linking it to a following noun ('the consequence of …').
7.root: و-ب-ل (w-b-l) — to be heavy, harmful, grievous

8.meaning: A compound: 'their affair' / 'their matter' / 'their command' — the word 'amr' (a matter, affair, command, or situation) joined to the pronoun 'their.'
8.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, which appears when the word follows a preposition or is possessed/linked to another word ('… of …'). The suffix '-him' is 'their' (masculine plural); its vowel is 'i' (not '-hum') precisely because it follows the genitive '-i.'

9.meaning: 'And for them / and they have.' A combination expressing possession or entitlement belonging to a group of males: 'and to/for them (belongs).' The particle li- conveys 'for' or 'belonging to,' and the attached pronoun refers to 'them.'
9.grammar: A possessive/benefactive phrase: the preposition li- ('for, belonging to') with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them,' masculine plural). Such 'for X' phrases commonly express that something belongs to or is owed to that party.

10.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
10.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

11.meaning: Painful, agonizing, deeply hurtful. An intensive adjective describing something that inflicts severe, grievous pain.
11.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl, conveying a strong, abiding quality ('truly painful'). The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the case of a subject or of a noun's basic naming form), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.

1.meaning: An expression meaning 'like the likeness of' or 'as the example of.' It joins the comparison word 'ka' (like, as) to the noun for a likeness/parable, setting up a comparison: 'comparable to the case of…'
1.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like, as') prefixed to a noun. Because ka- functions like a preposition, the noun takes the -i genitive ending, the case used after prepositions and to link 'the likeness OF …' to a following noun.

2.meaning: The Shayṭān — Satan, the devil: a rebellious, evil being who tempts and misleads; the term suggests one who is far removed from goodness and burning in defiance.
2.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the Satan / the devil'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
2.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote (from good/mercy); a devil

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

4.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
4.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

5.meaning: 'To / for mankind' — the collective noun 'humankind, the human being' preceded by the preposition 'to/for', expressing that something belongs to, is directed at, or is owed to humanity.
5.grammar: The noun 'the human being / mankind' with the definite article 'al-', governed by the preposition 'li-' ('to/for'). The final -i is genitive, the case required after a preposition; so the whole means 'to/for mankind'.

6.meaning: Disbelieve! — the Form I imperative of kafara (to disbelieve, to cover over, to be ungrateful); a command to disbelieve, spoken in context as a quotation of a tempting voice.
6.grammar: A Form I imperative, second person masculine singular; the -i or -u vowel on the final consonant marks it as imperative. The hamzat al-waṣl (connecting alif) begins the form. This is an aorist/imperative form of kafara.
6.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, to disbelieve, to be ungrateful; the verb kafara means to disbelieve; the noun kāfir means disbeliever

7.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
7.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

8.meaning: He disbelieved / rejected — to refuse faith, deny the truth, and turn away ungratefully from Allah. The root also carries the sense of covering over or being ungrateful for a blessing.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he disbelieved'). The final -a ending marks completed past action done by a single male. The verb denotes rejecting faith and being ungrateful, covering over the truth.
8.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject faith, be ungrateful

9.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
9.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

10.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
10.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

11.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'free of / quit of / disassociated from' — innocent of and having nothing to do with something, washing one's hands of it. It describes a person clear and detached from a thing, especially a wrong.
11.grammar: A descriptive noun, indefinite, with the nominative -un ending (tanwīn). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('[someone] is free/quit'); the -un tanwīn shows it is indefinite. It is usually completed by 'of/from' something.
11.root: ب-ر-ء (b-r-ʾ) — to be free, clear, quit of; innocence, disassociation

12.meaning: From You — origin or source traced back to a single addressee ('You'), as in a gift or sending that comes 'from You'.
12.grammar: The preposition min ('from') with an attached pronoun 'you' (masculine singular). Attached pronouns after a preposition are the object of that preposition; here it conveys 'from you'.

13.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
13.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

14.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
15.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

16.meaning: Lord, Master, Sustainer — the One who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings a thing to its completion; far richer than 'lord', it joins ownership, care, and continual upbringing of all that He sustains.
16.grammar: A noun ending in -a, marking the accusative case — the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb (e.g. of 'I fear') or when it is being addressed/specified into that case. It carries no prefix or article in this form.
16.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, lord over

17.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
17.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
17.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: So he became / so he was — the past-tense of 'to be,' often marking a transition into a state or the outcome of what preceded ('and so he came to be').
1.grammar: The past-tense verb 'to be' prefixed with 'fa-' ('so, then'). With no added ending, the bare form takes a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), describing a completed state or its result.
1.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

2.meaning: The end/outcome of both of them — ʿāqiba refers to the final consequence or end; the dual suffix -humā indicates two people; the accusative marks it as the object.

parts.en: the end / the outcome / the final consequence

2.grammar: A feminine noun (active participle form used as a noun: 'the follower / what comes after') in the accusative case, as the object of the verb 'to know' or similar. The dual possessive pronoun -humā ('of the two') refers to the two mentioned parties.
2.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow after; the noun ʿāqiba means the final outcome or end result; ʿāqibatahumā is 'the end of the two of them'

3.meaning: That they two … — the particle 'that/indeed' used to introduce and emphasize a statement, fused with the dual pronoun 'they two' as its subject.
3.grammar: The emphatic particle anna ('that, indeed') with the attached dual pronoun -humā ('they two') functioning as its subject. Anna introduces a noun clause and lends emphasis; it grammatically governs its subject in the accusative, here filled by the pronoun.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
5.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

6.meaning: Abiding forever, dwelling permanently — the dual active participle of khalada (to remain permanently); here in the dual form, referring to two people dwelling in the fire forever.
6.grammar: A masculine dual active participle in the genitive case (or accusative, as -ayni is the genitive/accusative dual ending, as opposed to nominative -āni). Dual form refers to the two people mentioned in the verse.
6.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — to be permanent, to abide forever; the active participle khālid means one who remains permanently; the dual khālidayni means the two who remain forever

7.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
7.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

8.meaning: 'And that' — a connective 'and' plus the demonstrative 'that', pointing to something distant or already mentioned (masculine).
8.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine singular demonstrative pronoun, 'that (one)'. Demonstratives in Arabic do not change for grammatical case; the -ka element is a particle directing attention to a distant referent.

9.meaning: Recompense, requital, reward or penalty — the fitting return given for a deed, whether good or evil; the due 'payback' that a deed earns.
9.grammar: A noun ending in -u, marking the nominative case — the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being described/identified ('the recompense is...'). It carries no article in this form, so it reads indefinitely as 'a recompense'.

10.meaning: Of the wrongdoers, of the transgressors — the masculine sound plural active participle of ẓalama (to wrong, oppress, transgress); in the genitive case after a preposition.
10.grammar: A masculine sound plural noun in the genitive case; the -īna ending (-ī + na) marks genitive/accusative plural (nominative would be -ūna). The definite article makes it 'the wrongdoers' specifically.
10.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress, be unjust; the active participle ẓālim means a wrongdoer; the plural ẓālimīn means the wrongdoers

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: Be mindful and wary of — guard yourselves by placing a protective barrier between yourselves and harm or wrongdoing. This is the verb of taqwā: God-conscious caution that shields one from what is forbidden.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group ('you all'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you.' Built on a reflexive pattern (Form VIII), it conveys 'protect yourselves / be on guard.'

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: And let (him/her/it) look — the wāw + lam al-amr (command lam) + verb in jussive: 'and let (a soul) look'. Expresses a third-person command.
6.grammar: Wāw is connective. Lam al-amr (the lam of command) takes the following verb in the jussive mood, expressing a third-person imperative: 'let it look'. Tanẓur is Form I jussive, third person feminine singular (agreeing with nafs, 'soul', which is feminine).
6.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, consider; the verb naẓara/yanẓuru means to look or to contemplate; here in the jussive for a third-person command

7.meaning: A soul, self, or person — the inner self of a living being; by extension, an individual.
7.grammar: A singular feminine noun, indefinite ('a soul'). The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative case, which typically marks the subject or doer.

8.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
8.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

9.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she/it put forward / sent ahead / advanced beforehand' — to send something on ahead, often used of deeds a person has done in advance and dispatched before themselves.
9.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in an intensive pattern (doubled middle letter) that conveys deliberately putting something forward. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it sent ahead'.
9.root: ق-د-م (q-d-m) — coming before, advancing, putting forward

10.meaning: For tomorrow, for the next day — lighadin: the preposition li- ('for') + ghadin ('tomorrow, the morrow'); used here in a broader sense of 'what is ahead' or 'the future'.
10.grammar: Li- is a preposition of purpose ('for'). Ghadin is a masculine noun in the genitive case, indefinite; the -in ending (tanwīn kasra) marks it genitive indefinite. Together lighadin means 'for tomorrow'.
10.root: غ-د-و (gh-d-w) — to go forth in the morning; the noun ghad means tomorrow; here used broadly for the near or ultimate future

11.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'guard yourselves / be mindful and on your guard.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself by being conscious of Allah and shielding oneself from wrongdoing and its consequences.
11.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you (all).' The -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressees ('you all'). The pattern (form VIII, from waqā 'to protect') gives the sense of taking protective care for oneself.
11.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
12.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

13.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
13.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
14.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

15.meaning: 'Fully aware / All-Aware' — one who knows the inner reality and hidden details of things through intimate, expert knowledge. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect awareness of all that is concealed.
15.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, thorough quality ('thoroughly aware'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamm): it marks an indefinite noun/adjective in the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.

16.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
16.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

17.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
17.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: You (plural) are / you happen to be. A form of the 'hollow' verb kāna ('to be'), which links a subject to a state or description, or expresses simply being or existing.
2.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The dropping of the usual final -na (so takūnū rather than takūnūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form expected after conditional or subordinating particles.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

3.meaning: Like those who — a comparison particle joined to a relative pronoun, meaning 'similar to the ones who…' and pointing to a group defined by what follows.
3.grammar: A compound of the preposition ka- ('like, as'), expressing resemblance, and the masculine plural relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). The relative pronoun is fixed in form and introduces a description; it does not change for case.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'they forgot' or 'they neglected/abandoned.' The root spans both genuine forgetfulness and the willful neglect of something one chooses to put out of mind.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -ū marks a completed action by 'they' (masculine plural). The silent 'alif' written after the -ū is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: So He made them forget themselves — fa- ('so') + ansāhum ('He made them forget' + 'them'): a causative construction where Allah causes people to forget themselves as a consequence of forgetting Him.
6.grammar: Fa- marks the consequence. Ansā is a Form IV past-tense verb (ansā/yansī — to cause to forget), third person masculine singular; the defective final root letter gives the contracted form. The -hum is the third-person masculine plural object pronoun.
6.root: ن-س-ي (n-s-y) — to forget; Form IV ansā means to cause to forget, to make someone neglect; the fateful result of forgetting Allah is forgetting one's own soul

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
7.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

8.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
8.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

9.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
9.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

10.meaning: Those who defiantly disobey — the active participle 'fāsiq' (one who breaks away from obedience, transgressing moral and religious limits) in its sound masculine plural, with the definite article.
10.grammar: Definite ('al-') sound masculine plural active participle. The '-ūna' ending is the nominative (subject) form of the masculine plural, used when the word is the doer of an action or the subject of a sentence.
10.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to break away, depart from obedience; to act immorally

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: 'They are equal / it is the same' — to be on a par, level, or alike; to stand even with one another with no difference of value.
2.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it is equal'). The 'ya-' prefix marks a present action; the weak final letter (from the root's last 'w/y') appears as the long ending. It expresses things being on the same level.
2.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — equality, levelness, being even/straight

3.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
3.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

4.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
4.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

5.meaning: And the companions of … / people belonging to … — 'companions' meaning those associated with, owners of, or people characterized by whatever follows.
5.grammar: Connector wa- ('and') plus the plural noun 'companions/associates'. The -u ending is nominative, typically marking the subject or the thing being identified. In the construct ('companions OF …') it leads into a following noun defining whom they belong to.
5.root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — companionship, accompanying, being associated with

6.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
6.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
6.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

7.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
7.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

8.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
8.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
8.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

9.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
9.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

10.meaning: The triumphant, the winners — those who attain what they sought and are saved from what they feared; the truly successful who achieve ultimate salvation and reward.
10.grammar: An active participle ('one who triumphs') with the article 'al-' ('the'), in the masculine plural. The '-ūna' ending marks the nominative plural — the case typically used for the subject or predicate of a sentence ('they are the triumphant').
10.root: ف-و-ز (f-w-z) — to succeed, triumph, win salvation, attain

1.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

2.meaning: We sent down — to cause something to descend or be revealed from a higher source to a lower; classically used of revelation sent down from on high.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb of the causative (fourth) form, meaning to make something come down. The attached -nā is the subject pronoun 'we', marking the action as completed and done by a 'we' (a form of majestic/collective speech when used of Allah).
2.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, be sent down

3.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
3.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

4.meaning: The Qur'an — the recited Scripture; literally 'the Recitation' or 'the Reading'.
4.grammar: A definite noun (carrying 'al-', 'the') on the verbal-noun pattern fuʿlān, denoting the act/thing of reciting. The final '-a' marks the accusative case, which most often signals that the word is the direct object of a verb.
4.root: ق-ر-ء (q-r-ʾ) — reciting, reading aloud, gathering words together

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

6.meaning: 'Mountain' or 'hill' — a large natural elevation of the earth.
6.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-in' ending (genitive with the doubled final 'n' of indefiniteness, 'tanwīn') signals 'a mountain' (not 'the') and is the case that regularly follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding one in a possessive ('… of a …') relationship.
6.root: ج-ب-ل (j-b-l) — mountain

7.meaning: Surely you would have seen it — the emphatic la- + ra-ayta + object pronoun -hu: a conditional apodosis ('if the Quran had been revealed on a mountain, you would certainly have seen it…').

parts.en: you (sg.) saw / you would have seen

7.grammar: The assertive lam + past-tense verb creates a counterfactual: 'you would surely have seen'. Raʾayta is Form I past tense, second person masculine singular (-ta suffix). The -hu is the third-person masculine singular object pronoun.
7.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see; the verb raʾā/yarā means to see; the past tense raʾayta is 'you saw'

8.meaning: Humbled, bowed in awe — the active participle of khashiʿa (to be humble, to be reverent in awe, to submit before a power greater than oneself); here in the accusative as a state of the mountain.
8.grammar: A masculine active participle (ism al-fāʿil) in the accusative case, indefinite; the -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) marks accusative indefinite, functioning as a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) describing the mountain's state.
8.root: خ-ش-ع (kh-sh-ʿ) — to be humble, submissive, reverently bowed; the verb khashiʿa and its participle khāshiʿ describe humble submission, especially before Allah

9.meaning: Splitting asunder, cracking apart — the active participle of Form V taṣaddaʿa (to crack, split, fracture); here describing the mountain splitting under the weight of the Quran.
9.grammar: A masculine active participle (Form V: mutafaʿʿil) in the accusative case, indefinite; the -an ending marks accusative indefinite ḥāl (circumstantial state). Form V of the root indicates an intensive, reflexive splitting.
9.root: ص-د-ع (ṣ-d-ʿ) — to crack, split, shatter; Form V taṣaddaʿa means to crack or split apart (reflexive-intensive); the participle mutaṣaddiʿ means splitting or cracking

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

11.meaning: Fear, awe, or reverent dread — an apprehension mingled with reverence, especially the awe felt before something great or holy.
11.grammar: A feminine singular verbal noun; the tā' marbūṭa (ة) belongs to the stem, with only the case diacritic split off. The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('fear OF …') or follows a preposition. As a verbal noun it can also convey reason or motive ('out of fear').
11.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — to fear with awe, dread reverently

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: And that; and that one. 'Tilka' is a demonstrative pointing to something distant or notable ('that' / 'those'), prefixed with 'and'. It singles out and draws attention to a thing set apart.
13.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a feminine demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' or 'those'. As a demonstrative it is fixed in form (it does not change for case) and serves to point out and identify something at a distance.

14.meaning: Examples, parables, likenesses — the plural of mathal (an example, parable, or likeness used to illustrate a point); in the nominative case as the subject.
14.grammar: A masculine broken plural noun in the nominative case; the -u ending marks it as the subject (nominative). Amthāl is the broken plural of mathal. The definite article makes it 'the examples' (i.e., these specific parables).
14.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to be like, to resemble; the noun mathal means an example or parable; its plural amthāl refers to the examples or parables struck for understanding

15.meaning: We present them / We strike them (as parables) — naḍribu + hā ('we strike them'); the idiom ḍaraba mathal means 'to give an example/parable'.
15.grammar: A Form I present/imperfect verb, first person plural; the -u ending marks indicative mood. The -hā is the third-person feminine singular (or feminine plural) object pronoun, referring back to the amthāl (examples — which can take feminine pronouns in Arabic). The idiom naḍribu amthāl means 'we give parables/examples'.
15.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — to strike, hit, travel; the idiom ḍaraba mathal means to present a parable or example; naḍribuhā means 'we present them'

16.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
16.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

17.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

17.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.

18.meaning: They reflect / ponder — to think deeply and turn a matter over in the mind, considering it carefully.
18.grammar: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'they reflect.' The intensive pattern (with the doubled middle root letter) conveys careful, repeated mental effort. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural doer ('they') in the ordinary (indicative) mood.

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
2.root: — (proper divine name)

3.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
5.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
5.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

6.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
6.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
6.root: — (particle)

7.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
7.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

8.meaning: Knower — the active participle 'one who knows,' describing someone characterized by knowledge. Applied to Allah it conveys the One who fully knows all things.
8.grammar: Active participle (a noun describing the doer), masculine singular: 'a knower / knowing one.' The long vowel after the first letter is the participle pattern. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the subject of a sentence or a noun standing on its own.

9.meaning: The unseen / the hidden realm — that which lies beyond perception and human knowledge: the realm and matters concealed from the senses, known fully only to Allah.
9.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al-. The final -i is the genitive ending, which marks the word as following a preposition or as the second term in a possessive link ('… of the unseen').
9.root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b) — to be absent, hidden, beyond perception

10.meaning: And the witnessed / the seen — joined by 'and,' this is the realm of what is visible, present, and openly perceived; the opposite of the hidden or unseen. (The word also carries the senses of testimony and witnessing.)
10.grammar: 'and' + definite feminine noun. The wa- prefix means 'and,' al- means 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically appearing after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun.
10.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, be present, testify

11.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
11.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

12.meaning: The Most Gracious / All-Merciful (al-Raḥmān) — a name of Allah from the root of mercy, in an intensive pattern denoting mercy that is vast, all-encompassing, and overflowing to all creation.
12.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'r', written al-raḥmān, said ar-raḥmān). An intensive noun-form expressing immense, overflowing mercy. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking a subject, predicate, or name in apposition to such.

13.meaning: A name/quality meaning 'the Most Merciful' or 'the Bestower of mercy' — the One whose mercy is deeply felt and continually shown to His creation.
13.grammar: The definite article l- ('the') with an intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality of mercy. The -u ending marks nominative case, typical of a subject or of a word describing/identifying the subject.

8.meaning: The Sovereign, the King — al-malik is one of the divine names; it denotes absolute sovereignty, dominion, and authority over all creation.
8.grammar: A masculine noun in the nominative case; the -u ending marks it as the subject or predicate of the clause (huwa l-maliku: 'He is the Sovereign'). The definite article establishes it as a divine name.
8.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, to possess, to reign; the noun malik means king/sovereign; as a divine name it means the absolute Sovereign

9.meaning: The Holy One, the Most Pure — al-quddūs is a divine name denoting absolute holiness and freedom from all imperfection; the form (fuʿʿūl) intensifies the quality to the highest degree.

parts.en: the Holy One / the Most Pure

9.grammar: A masculine noun (intensive form: fuʿʿūl) in the nominative case; the -u ending marks predicative nominative. As a divine name it is always definite (al-quddūs).
9.root: ق-د-س (q-d-s) — to be holy, pure, sacred; the noun quddūs is the intensive form meaning the supremely holy, utterly pure one

10.meaning: The Giver of Peace, the Source of Safety — al-salām as a divine name means Allah is the source and essence of peace and safety; the name al-Salām also means that Allah is free from all faults and imperfections.

parts.en: the (Giver of) Peace / the Source of Safety

10.grammar: A masculine noun in the nominative case; the -u ending marks predicative nominative. The definite article is inherent to the divine name.
10.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — to be safe, sound, peaceful; the noun salām means peace, safety, wholeness; as a divine name it indicates Allah as the source and embodiment of safety and peace

11.meaning: The Giver of Security, the Bestower of Faith — al-muʾmin as a divine name means the One who grants security and safety, or who attests to the truth of His messengers; the root also gives the word for 'believer'.

parts.en: the Giver of Security / the Granter of Iman

11.grammar: A masculine active participle (Form IV ism al-fāʿil) in the nominative case; the -u ending marks predicative nominative. As a divine name, al-muʾmin means the One who bestows security and safety (or who confirms truth).
11.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to believe; Form IV āmana/yuʾminu means to bestow security or to believe; as a divine name it means the Granter of Safety/Security

12.meaning: The Guardian, the Watcher, the Overseer — al-muhayminu as a divine name means the One who watches over, guards, and has complete dominion and authority over all things.

parts.en: the Guardian / the Watcher / the Overseer

12.grammar: A masculine active participle in the nominative case; the -u ending marks predicative nominative. The form (mufayʿil) suggests an intensive watching or guarding function.
12.root: ه-ي-م-ن (h-y-m-n) — to watch over, to guard; some derive it from amina (security); the divine name al-muhayminu denotes ultimate guardianship and oversight

13.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
13.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

14.meaning: The Irresistible, the Compeller, the One who overcomes all obstacles — al-jabbār as a divine name means Allah whose will cannot be resisted or thwarted; He compels all things to His will, and He restores (jabara) the broken.

parts.en: the Irresistible / the Compeller / the One whose will is absolute

14.grammar: A masculine intensive noun (faʿʿāl pattern) in the nominative case; the -u ending marks predicative nominative. The faʿʿāl pattern expresses an intensified quality.
14.root: ج-ب-ر (j-b-r) — to set a broken bone, to compel, to be mighty; the noun jabbār in human contexts can mean tyrant, but as a divine name it means the Irresistible whose will prevails over all things

15.meaning: The Supreme, the Possessor of Greatness — al-mutakabbiru as a divine name means the One who rightfully claims all greatness to Himself; unlike human arrogance (kibr), divine kibriyāʾ is the appropriate majesty of the Creator.

parts.en: the Supreme / the Possessor of Greatness

15.grammar: A masculine active participle (Form V: mutafaʿʿil) in the nominative case; the -u ending marks predicative nominative. Form V of the root conveys a reflexive claiming of greatness — uniquely appropriate for Allah alone.
15.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great, large; Form V takabbara means to claim greatness for oneself; as a divine name al-mutakabbiru means the One who rightfully possesses and claims all greatness

16.meaning: An exclamation declaring Allah utterly free of every flaw, partner, or imperfection — 'Glory be! / How perfect He is!' It is a noun of glorification used to affirm absolute transcendence and purity.
16.grammar: A verbal noun in the accusative case, marked by the -a ending; it functions as an exclamation typically followed by a noun in the genitive ('Glory be to …'). It conveys the act of declaring someone free of any defect.
16.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide; figuratively to declare free of imperfection

17.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
17.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

18.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
18.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

19.meaning: 'They associate (partners with Him)' — an ongoing/present verb. From the root for partnership, this form (causative, Form IV) means to make something a partner or associate, especially to set up partners alongside Allah in worship or divinity (the act underlying shirk).
19.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' doing the action now or habitually. The yu- prefix is the marker of Form IV (causative): 'to make (something) a partner.' The full -ūna ending signals the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state, not cut short by a governing particle.
19.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; (causative) to associate partners

4.grammar: A masculine active participle (Form I) in the nominative case; the -u ending marks predicative nominative. The final hamza is part of the root.
4.root: ب-ر-أ (b-r-ʾ) — to create with distinction, to free from; the verb bāraʾa/barāʾa means to create distinctly separated beings; as a divine name al-bāriʾ is the One who originates each creature in its distinct form

5.meaning: The Fashioner of Forms, the Shaper — al-muṣawwiru as a divine name means the One who gives each created being its distinctive shape, image, and form; He is the artist of creation who determines how each thing looks.

parts.en: the Fashioner / the Shaper of Forms

5.grammar: A masculine active participle (Form II: mufaʿʿil) in the nominative case; the -u ending marks predicative nominative. Form II (ṣawwara/yuṣawwiru) means to fashion or shape; the tashdīd on the wāw intensifies the creative shaping.

6.meaning: To him / for him / he has — the preposition 'to/for' fused with a pronoun meaning 'him.' It expresses belonging, benefit, or possession (something is 'his' or done 'for him').
6.grammar: A preposition 'li-/la-' ('to, for') with the attached 3rd-person masculine singular pronoun 'him.' The pairing means 'to him' or 'for him' and often conveys possession ('he has …') or that an action is directed toward his benefit or detriment.
6.root: — (particle with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: The names — the plural of 'name'; the words or titles by which something is called.
7.grammar: A definite plural noun: 'the names.' The -u ending is the nominative case, typically marking the word as a subject or as the thing being described (predicate).

8.meaning: The best, the finest, the most beautiful (feminine form) — the supremely good outcome or reward; goodness in its highest degree.
8.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in the feminine superlative pattern ('the best, the finest'). Its long final 'ā' is a fixed ending that does not change for case; it denotes the utmost degree of goodness and often names the best reward or recompense.

9.meaning: 'He / it glorifies, declares free of all imperfection' — a present-tense verb proclaiming Allah's absolute transcendence above every flaw.
9.grammar: Present-tense verb in the intensive (form II) pattern. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he / it'). The final -u is the indicative mood, signalling a plain, ongoing statement of fact. The verb means to extol Allah as utterly beyond any imperfection or likeness.
9.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide; to declare Allah free of all imperfection

10.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
10.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
13.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

14.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
14.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

15.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
15.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

16.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
16.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

17.meaning: "the All-Wise" — one full of wisdom, who judges and orders everything with perfect, sound judgement; as a divine name 'al-Ḥakīm' denotes the One whose every act and decree is supremely wise.
17.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, abiding quality ('ever-wise'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes as the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description.
17.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, govern; wisdom
